title: Void Ending in a Trine to Saturn
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3, Book III chapter 1 and Book III chapter 8

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Saturn, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his weight and his cold. Saturn holds the power of retention, and when he is afflicted he is the gravest of the impediments: the science of law and profound knowledge, deep and occult properties, the building trades, and working the soil are his, with murky rivers, black mountains, deep wells, and desert places among his locations. Lead and iron are his metals, black his color, the bitter taste his own. Well disposed and direct, he gives purity, long life, standing, honor, riches, and durable inheritances; afflicted, he is the lord of poverty, misery, pain, and imprisonment.
